cards.text: Jesus is surrounded by a crowd. A BIG one. Then some visitors show up wanting to see Him, and these aren't strangers, friend: they've known Him for years.

cards.question: Who comes to see Jesus while the crowd is packed around Him?
Jesus' mother and brothers make their way through the crowd and walk right up to Him.

cards.text: So somebody passes a message to Jesus through all those people, like the world's slowest group chat. And it's about His family.

cards.question: Jesus is told that His mother and brothers are standing ___ wanting to see Him.
Jesus answers. Who does He say His mother and brothers are?

answers.text: Those who hear God's word and carry it out
Those who follow Him from town to town
Those who sit closest to Him and listen

cards.question: According to Jesus, hearing the word of God is enough to be His family, even without carrying it out.

findings.problem: The right answer is one word ("outside"), but the wrong answers are three words ("on the shore" and "by the well"). This length gap makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The opening card reads as pleasant scene-setting with no real laugh. "A BIG one" and "these aren't strangers, friend" are mild. Card 1 is one of only two story cards in the walkthrough, so it is one of the few places Papa Dorin's humor can show. It should push for a real laugh.

rule.text: Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
